events.title: Geoffrey Hinton's team wins ImageNet with AlexNet
events.summary: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton submitted AlexNet to ILSVRC 2012 on September 30, 2012 — winning with 15.3% top-5 error and triggering the deep learning revolution.
events.about: AlexNet's GPU-trained convolutional network crushed traditional computer vision pipelines — convincing Google, Facebook, and industry to bet on neural networks. Hinton had pursued backprop for decades before this breakthrough.

narrative.whyChosen: AlexNet was the inflection point for modern deep learning adoption.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved neural networks could beat hand-engineered vision features at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Computer vision relied on brittle handcrafted features that did not generalize.

events.title: Joomla 3.0 released
events.summary: The Joomla project shipped Joomla 3.0 on September 27, 2012 — a Bootstrap-based admin UI and mobile-ready front-end templates.
events.about: Joomla 3 brought responsive templates, a modernized media manager, and improved ACL — aligning the CMS with mobile-first expectations. It followed the short-term release strategy before Joomla settled on longer support cycles in the 3.x era.

narrative.whyChosen: Joomla 3 modernized the admin experience with Bootstrap and responsive design.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept Joomla competitive as mobile traffic overtook desktop browsing.
narrative.problemSolved: Joomla 2.5's admin and default templates felt dated on phones and tablets.
